key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a proven upper bound of 5(n−1) rounds, closing the gap to the known Ω(n) lower bound.
engineering_relevance: This gives a sharper worst-case guarantee for graph isomorphism-related refinement methods, which matters for scalable graph analytics, symmetry detection, and ML pipelines using WL-style features.
method: Analyze color refinement dynamics for pairs of vertices (2-WL).
Derive a global upper bound on stabilization rounds using combinatorial arguments.
Extend the approach to k-dimensional WL for k≥3, yielding improved iteration bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a new proven upper bound of 5(n−1) iterations for 2-WL, improving the prior O(n log n) bound and matching the asymptotic Ω(n) lower bound.
watch_item: The bound is about iteration count, not per-iteration runtime, so practical speedups still depend on implementation and graph size.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
